response.text:
I can’t give a precise percentage without the underlying data — I won’t fabricate numbers. If you can share the counts or let me access the data, I’ll compute it exactly. Otherwise I can show how to calculate it or produce an estimate based on assumptions you approve.

How to compute the renewal rate (exact)
- Formula: renewal % = (number of users who renewed during the quarter / number of users eligible to renew that quarter) × 100

Example (illustrative only)
- If 1,200 users renewed out of 5,000 eligible → renewal % = (1,200 / 5,000) × 100 = 24%

SQL (generic)
- SELECT 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN renewed THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS renewal_pct
  FROM subscriptions
  WHERE renewal_eligible_date BETWEEN '<quarter_start>' AND '<quarter_end>';

Spreadsheet
- = ( renewed_count / eligible_count ) * 100

If you want an estimate instead of an exact figure, tell me:
- Any prior renewal rate or benchmark to use, and
- Whether “last quarter” means the most recent calendar quarter or a fiscal quarter (and its dates).

Which would you like: compute exactly (provide the counts or dataset), or produce an estimate (give assumptions or benchmarks)?
